checked_claims.claim: Default _Unset() is allocated on every function invocation
checked_claims.reason: Python defaults are evaluated when function is defined, not every call; magnitude is unmeasured.

material_errors: Python defaults are evaluated when function is defined, not every call; magnitude is unmeasured.
tasks.notes: Direct static source review; no code run.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The module creates one shared UNSET sentinel (lib/matplotlib/_api/__init__.py:30-35). Reusing it avoids separate sentinel allocations and supplies a common identity for distinguishing omitted arguments from explicit None. However, def foo(arg=_Unset()) creates its default once at function definition, not once per call. Thousands of checks therefore do not imply thousands of new objects; only explicit per-call construction would create that allocation pattern.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Legend rejects simultaneous non-None title_fontsize/title_fontproperties, normalizes properties and applies size fallback before set_title (lib/matplotlib/legend.py:555-571). A reusable normalization helper with an explicit mutually-exclusive-parameters check could generalize this while preserving parameter-specific precedence. Do not automatically apply that rule to regular prop/fontsize: existing code gives prop precedence instead of rejecting both (lib/matplotlib/legend.py:429-434).

checked_claims.claim: chr(glyph) maps T1 code back to original Unicode character
checked_claims.reason: Subset expects encoding-array indices; chr/ord is code transport, not decoding T1 into Unicode.

material_errors: Subset expects encoding-array indices; chr/ord is code transport, not decoding T1 into Unicode.
tasks.notes: Direct static source review; no code run.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The test selects charter, T1 font encoding and UTF-8 input for accented text and ligatures (lib/matplotlib/tests/test_backend_pdf.py:470-479). PDF draw_tex writes bytes([glyph]) and tracks chr(glyph) (lib/matplotlib/backends/backend_pdf.py:2293-2299); tracking stores ord values (lib/matplotlib/backends/_backend_pdf_ps.py:109-113). These are font encoding indices, not decoded original Unicode characters. Embedding applies the map-file encoding before subsetting by tracked indices (lib/matplotlib/backends/backend_pdf.py:1018-1030; lib/matplotlib/_type1font.py:840-850).

checked_claims.claim: Undo-log trajectory updates are atomic and independent for concurrency
checked_claims.reason: Single shared _traj/_current_xy and immediate mask mutations do not provide concurrent isolation; adaptive implications omitted.

material_errors: Single shared _traj/_current_xy and immediate mask mutations do not provide concurrent isolation; adaptive implications omitted.
tasks.notes: Direct static source review; no code run.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: StreamMask uses _traj as an undo log: entering an unoccupied cell records it and immediately marks _mask; undo clears logged cells (lib/matplotlib/streamplot.py:453-478). This supports serial rejection of a tentative trajectory. It is not a concurrency-safe transaction: one shared trajectory list/current position and mutable mask would require per-trajectory ownership and synchronization for concurrent generation. Adaptive changes to mask resolution would also need to preserve or remap recorded cell indices; the existing fixed-density grid does not provide that mechanism (lib/matplotlib/streamplot.py:437-448).

checked_claims.reason: Method explicitly reads axis tick-space/minpos when attached; tests do not enforce strict separation.

material_errors: Method explicitly reads axis tick-space/minpos when attached; tests do not enforce strict separation.
tasks.notes: Direct static source review; no code run.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: LogLocator.__call__ gets the axis view interval and delegates to tick_values (lib/matplotlib/ticker.py:2401-2404). tick_values can operate without an axis for valid explicit bounds, using nine automatic ticks, but is not purely axis-independent: attached axes provide tick space and a replacement minimum positive value (lib/matplotlib/ticker.py:2414-2427). nonsingular also considers shared axes minimum positive values (lib/matplotlib/ticker.py:2547-2564). Standalone versus axes tests exercise both uses; they do not enforce a strict pure-core/integration boundary.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: test_pdflatex sets pgf.texsystem=pdflatex, font options and preamble via mpl.rcParams.update, then calls create_figure in the same test module (lib/matplotlib/tests/test_backend_pgf.py:103-110). That helper builds lines, markers, filled paths and text (lib/matplotlib/tests/test_backend_pgf.py:49-77). The image_comparison decorator then saves/compares output; PGF rendering and TeX compilation are implemented deeper in FigureCanvasPgf, including _print_pgf_to_fh and print_pdf in lib/matplotlib/backends/backend_pgf.py.

checked_claims.claim: Alignment offset calculation lives inside Text.get_window_extent
checked_claims.reason: These lines belong to _get_layout, defined at 360; get_window_extent calls it at 985.

material_errors: These lines belong to _get_layout, defined at 360; get_window_extent calls it at 985.
tasks.notes: Direct static source review; no code run.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Text._get_layout computes alignment-dependent offsetx/offsety, including xtick/ytick rotation modes (lib/matplotlib/text.py:360,454-508). Text.get_window_extent invokes _get_layout to obtain its bounding box (lib/matplotlib/text.py:984-986). Axis._get_ticklabel_bboxes calls visible labels get_window_extent (lib/matplotlib/axis.py:1333-1338), and axis drawing/layout operations use that helper. The calculation is therefore reached through get_window_extent but is not defined inside it.
